label: Galilean satellites
definition: Jupiter's four large moons, Io (I), Europa (II), Ganymede (III) and Callisto (IV), discovered by Galileo in 1610. They orbit close to Jupiter's equatorial plane at about 5.9, 9.4, 15.0 and 26.3 Jupiter radii.

label: Jupiter's shadow
definition: The umbral and penumbral cones cast by Jupiter away from the Sun. At the Galilean satellites the umbra is barely narrower than Jupiter and the penumbra is a rim about 750 to 3400 km wide.

label: eclipse of a satellite
definition: The passage of a satellite through Jupiter's shadow. It depends only on the Sun's direction. Disappearance (EC D) and reappearance (EC R) are timed at half the satellite's normal light.

label: occultation by Jupiter
definition: The passage of a satellite behind Jupiter's disc as seen from the Earth. Disappearance (OC D) and reappearance (OC R) are timed when the limb bisects the satellite.

label: transit of a satellite
definition: The passage of a satellite in front of Jupiter's disc as seen from the Earth, from ingress (TR I) to egress (TR E).

label: PHEMU campaign
definition: An international campaign, coordinated by IMCCE, to record light curves of mutual events of the Galilean satellites in one equinox season. Named by year, for example PHEMU15 for 2014 to 2015.

label: jovicentric declination of the Earth or Sun
definition: The latitude of the Earth (D_E) or the Sun (D_S) above Jupiter's equatorial plane as seen from Jupiter's centre. It stays within about 4 degrees, and it crosses zero at each Jovian equinox.

label: satellite X, Y coordinates
definition: The apparent offset of a satellite from Jupiter's centre in the sky plane, in units of Jupiter's equatorial radius, with X along Jupiter's equator and Y towards Jupiter's north pole. The same offsets seen from the Sun decide eclipses and shadow transits.

label: Jupiter's flattening
definition: The fractional difference between Jupiter's equatorial and polar radii, $(71492-66854)/71492 = 0.0649$ with the IAU 2015 radii. It makes the disc and the shadow ellipses about 6.5 per cent shorter north to south.

label: differential light-time
definition: The correction for a satellite being nearer to or farther from the Earth than Jupiter, so that its light left at a slightly different time. In Meeus's form it shifts X by $|Z|/K$ times a geometric factor, with K close to the speed of light divided by the satellite's orbital speed.

label: phase correction
definition: The shift in a predicted contact caused by Jupiter's terminator not coinciding with its limb when the Sun and Earth directions differ. Thuillot gives up to 3 minutes for Io and 6 minutes for Callisto near quadrature.

label: mid-event convention
definition: The rule that a published eclipse time is the instant of half flux, and an occultation, transit or shadow transit time the instant the limb or shadow edge bisects the satellite. A visual observer sees the last or first speck instead, a minute or more away.

label: Sampson-Lieske theory
definition: The analytical theory of the Galilean satellites built by Sampson (1921) and redeveloped by Lieske (1977) with 49 adjustable constants. Its fits E-1 to E5 and Arlot's G-5 underlie most predictions made before about 2014.

label: Hapke model
definition: A physical model of how a rough, porous surface scatters light as a function of incidence, emission and phase angles. Mutual-event fits use it, or the Oren-Nayar model, to set the brightness distribution across a satellite's disc.

label: refractive tail
definition: The slow final fading of an eclipse light curve caused by sunlight refracted and scattered through Jupiter's atmosphere into the geometric shadow. It lasts minutes at red and near-infrared wavelengths.
